mission.title: kyverno: Reports controller fails to create events and policy expression error after upgrade to 3.5.1
mission.description: Reports controller fails to create events and policy expression error after upgrade to 3.5.1. This issue affects 19+ users.

steps.title: Identify kyverno troubleshoot symptoms
steps.description:
Check for the issue in your kyverno deployment:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n kyverno -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kyverno
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kyverno -n kyverno --tail=100 | grep -i error
```
Look for error: `no such key: username`

steps.title: Review kyverno configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant kyverno configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n kyverno -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kyverno
kubectl get configmap -n kyverno -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=kyverno
```
## Environment
- **Kyverno Version**: Upgraded from 3.4.4 to 3.5.1
- **Kubernetes Platform**: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)
- **Component**: kyverno-reports-controller

## Problem Description

After upgrading Kyverno from version 3.4.4 to 3.5.1,

steps.title: Apply the fix for Reports controller fails to create events and policy…
steps.description:
Partially fixes #14281.

When the reports controller background-scans native `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` and `MutatingAdmissionPolicy` resources, any policy that references `request.userInfo.username` fails with `no such key: username`. The most common case is GKE's built-in
```yaml
expression '![ "system:addon-manager", "system:serviceaccount:kube-system:cronjob-controller", ... ].exists(sa, sa == request.userInfo.username)' resulted in error: no such key: username
```

steps.title: Confirm Reports controller fails to create events and… is resolved
steps.description:
Verify the fix by checking that the original error no longer occurs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kyverno -n kyverno --tail=50 --since=5m
kubectl get events -n kyverno --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm that `no such key: username` no longer appears in logs.

resolution.summary:
Partially fixes #14281.

When the reports controller background-scans native `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` and `MutatingAdmissionPolicy` resources, any policy that references `request.userInfo.username` fails with `no such key: username`. The most common case is GKE's built-in `validating-node-p4sa-audience` VAP (present on GKE >= 1.32), which users can't modify to add a `has()` guard.
codeSnippets: expression '![ "system:addon-manager", "system:serviceaccount:kube-system:cronjob-controller", ... ].exists(sa, sa == request.userInfo.username)' resulted in error: no such key: username
